sentences.en: Hi, my name's Joe Bernstein and I'm a reporter on the Styles Desk at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫乔·伯恩斯坦，是《纽约时报》风格版的一名记者。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday read is a story I wrote for our magazine about a 48-year-old man named Benjamin Bolger.
sentences.zh: 本周的“周日阅读”是我为杂志写的一篇报道，关于一位名叫本杰明·博尔格的48岁男子。

sentences.en: And what makes Benjamin special is that he is America's preeminent perpetual student.
sentences.zh: 本杰明之所以特别，是因为他是美国最杰出的“终身学生”。

sentences.en: That is, he's someone who collects college degrees.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他是一个热衷于收集大学学位的人。

sentences.en: Over the past 30 years, he's received over a dozen degrees.
sentences.zh: 在过去的30年里，他获得了十几多个学位。

sentences.en: They're from the world's most prestigious institutions.
sentences.zh: 它们来自世界上最负盛名的学府。

sentences.en: Harvard, Stanford, and Yale, just to name a few.
sentences.zh: 哈佛、斯坦福和耶鲁，仅举几例。

sentences.en: I had the same reaction as many people when they hear about Benjamin for the first time.
sentences.zh: 当许多人第一次听说本杰明时，我的反应和他们一样。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What would possess someone to dedicate themselves to this kind of life?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使一个人投身于这样的生活？

sentences.en: So, last summer, I decided to go to Boston and ask Benjamin myself.
sentences.zh: 所以，去年夏天，我决定去波士顿亲自问问本杰明。

sentences.en: And talking to him is almost like talking to a walking freshman seminar.
sentences.zh: 和他交谈，几乎就像是在和一个行走的大学新生研讨会对话。

sentences.en: We talked about union labor.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了工会劳工。

sentences.en: We talked about cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了加密货币。

sentences.en: We talked about the nature of bridges, international and Middle Eastern diplomacy, even Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了桥梁的本质、国际和中东外交，甚至圣女贞德。

sentences.en: And I asked him, basically a hundred different ways,
sentences.zh: 我基本上用了一百种不同的方式问他，

sentences.en: why can't you stop going to college?
sentences.zh: 为什么你不能停止上大学？

sentences.en: And his answer just kind of stunned me in its obviousness.
sentences.zh: 他的回答因其显而易见而让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: He told me,
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，

sentences.en: I love learning.
sentences.zh: 我热爱学习。

sentences.en: Higher education, as an institution writ large, is so contested today, both politically and culturally.
sentences.zh: 高等教育作为一个庞大的机构，在当今政治和文化上都备受争议。

sentences.en: People take out enormous amounts of debt.
sentences.zh: 人们背负着巨额债务。

sentences.en: And we know that a lot of these degrees may not set you up for life in the way we've been told.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，很多学位可能并不能像人们告诉我们的那样，为你的一生提供保障。

sentences.en: And so, when universities have this lofty rhetoric about learning how to think and how to be a complete person, but then most of their graduates
sentences.zh: 因此，当大学高谈阔论关于学习如何思考和如何成为一个完整的人时，大多数毕业生

sentences.en: are just going to earn some ungodly starting salary at a consulting firm anyways, I think it's natural to ask, what is the point?
sentences.zh: 反正还是要到咨询公司去赚取一份令人咋舌的起薪，我觉得问一句“意义何在”是很自然的。

sentences.en: Is the only reason to go to college to have that credential?
sentences.zh: 上大学的唯一理由就是为了那个证书吗？

sentences.en: Is the actual content less important than the paper that you're given when you graduate?
sentences.zh: 实际的内容是否比毕业时拿到的那张纸更不重要？

sentences.en: But then there's Benjamin,
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了本杰明，

sentences.en: someone who has so fully immersed themselves in the ethos of the elite university, deeper than anyone else.
sentences.zh: 一个比任何人都更深入地沉浸在精英大学精神内核中的人。

sentences.en: And maybe he just genuinely does enjoy learning.
sentences.zh: 也许他确实是真心热爱学习。

sentences.en: And for someone like him, maybe this was the right kind of way to live his life.
sentences.zh: 对于像他这样的人来说，这或许就是他生活方式的正确选择。

sentences.en: What could we learn from Benjamin?
sentences.zh: 我们能从本杰明身上学到什么？

sentences.en: So here's my article, read by Robert Petkoff.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章，由罗伯特·佩特科夫朗读。

sentences.zh: 我们的制片人是杰克·迪西多罗。

sentences.zh: 我们的音乐由亚伦·埃斯波西托创作并演奏。

sentences.zh: 本杰明·B·

sentences.en: Bulger has been to Harvard and Stanford and Yale.
sentences.zh: 博尔格去过哈佛、斯坦福和耶鲁。

sentences.en: He has been to Columbia and Dartmouth and Oxford and Cambridge, Brandeis, and Brown.
sentences.zh: 他去过哥伦比亚大学、达特茅斯学院、牛津大学、剑桥大学、布兰迪斯大学和布朗大学。

sentences.en: Overall, Bulger has 14 advanced degrees, plus an associate's and a bachelor's.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，博尔格拥有14个高级学位，外加一个副学士学位和一个学士学位。

sentences.en: Some of Bulger's degrees took many years to complete, such as a doctorate from the Harvard Graduate School of Design.
sentences.zh: 博尔格的一些学位花费了多年时间才完成，例如哈佛大学设计研究生院的博士学位。

sentences.en: Others have required rather less commitment, low-residency MFAs from Ashland University and the University of Tampa, for example.
sentences.zh: 另一些则需要较少的投入，例如阿什兰大学和坦帕大学的低驻留期艺术硕士学位。

sentences.en: Some produced microscopically specific research, like Bulger's Harvard dissertation, deliberative democratic design, participants' perception of strategy used
sentences.zh: 有些研究极其具体，比如博尔格的哈佛论文，关于审议式民主设计、参与者对审议式公共参与所用策略的感知，

sentences.en: for deliberative public participation, and the types of participant satisfaction generated from deliberative public participation in the design process.
sentences.zh: 以及在设计过程中，审议式公共参与所产生的参与者满意度类型。

sentences.en: Others have been more of a grab bag, such as a 2004 master's from Dartmouth, for which Bulger studied Iranian sociology and the poetry of Robert FroSt.
sentences.zh: 另一些则更像是一个大杂烩，比如他2004年从达特茅斯获得的硕士学位，当时博尔格研究的是伊朗社会学和罗伯特·弗罗斯特的诗歌。

sentences.en: He has degrees in international development, creative nonfiction, and education.
sentences.zh: 他拥有国际发展、创意非虚构写作和教育学学位。

sentences.en: He has studied conflict and coexistence under Mari Fitzduff, the Irish policymaker who mediated during the Troubles, and American architecture under the eminent historian
sentences.zh: 他曾在爱尔兰政策制定者玛丽·菲茨达夫的指导下学习冲突与共存，玛丽曾在北爱尔兰问题期间进行调解；他还曾在杰出历史学家

sentences.en: Gwendolyn Wright.
sentences.zh: 格温多琳·赖特的指导下学习美国建筑。

sentences.en: He is currently working remotely toward a master's in writing for performance from Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 他目前正在远程攻读剑桥大学的表演写作硕士学位。

sentences.en: Bulger is a broad man with lank, whitish, chin-length hair and a dignified profile, like a figure from an antique coin.
sentences.zh: 博尔格身材魁梧，留着稀疏、灰白、齐下巴的头发，侧脸轮廓庄重，就像古钱币上的人物。

sentences.en: One of his favorite places is Walden Pond.
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢的地方之一是瓦尔登湖。

sentences.en: He met his wife there on one of his early morning constitutionals, and as he expounds upon learning and nature, it is easy to imagine him back in Thoreau's time,
sentences.zh: 他在一次清晨散步时遇到了他的妻子，当他阐述学习与自然时，很容易让人想象他回到了梭罗的时代，

sentences.en: with all the other polymathic gentlemen, perhaps by lamplight, stroking their old-timey facial hair, considering propositions about a wide range of topics,
sentences.zh: 和其他博学的绅士们在一起，也许在灯光下，抚摸着他们老式的胡须，思考着各种各样的话题，

sentences.en: advancing theories of the life well-lived.
sentences.zh: 推进关于美好生活的理论。

sentences.en: And there's something almost anachronistically earnest, even romantic, about the reason he gives for spending the past 30-odd years pursuing college degrees.
sentences.zh: 他过去30多年来追求大学学位的理由，有一种近乎不合时宜的真诚，甚至浪漫。

sentences.en: I love learning, he told me over lunch last year, without even a touch of irony.
sentences.zh: “我热爱学习，”去年午餐时他对我说道，语气中没有一丝讽刺。

sentences.en: I had been pestering him for the better part of two days from every angle I could imagine to offer some deeper explanation for his life as a perpetual student.
sentences.zh: 在那之前的两天里，我一直从我能想到的各个角度纠缠他，希望他能为自己作为“终身学生”的生活提供更深层的解释。

sentences.en: Every time I tried and failed, I felt irredeemably 21st century, like an extra in a historical production who has forgotten to remove his Apple Watch.
sentences.zh: 每次我尝试失败后，我都感到自己无可救药地属于21世纪，就像一个历史剧里的临时演员忘了摘下他的Apple Watch。

sentences.en: I believe that people are like trees, he said.
sentences.zh: “我相信人就像树一样，”他说。

sentences.en: I hope I am a sequoia.
sentences.zh: “我希望我是一棵红杉。”

sentences.en: I want to grow for as long as possible and reach toward the highest level of the sky.
sentences.zh: “我想尽可能长久地生长，伸向天空的最高处。”

sentences.en: Against a backdrop of pervasive cynicism about the nature of higher education, it is tempting to dismiss a figure like Bulger as the wacky byproduct of an empty system.
sentences.zh: 在对高等教育本质普遍持怀疑态度的背景下，人们很容易将博尔格这样的人物视为一个空洞体制的古怪产物。

sentences.en: Then again, Bulger has run himself through that system over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，博尔格已经一次又一次地把自己投入到那个体制中。

sentences.en: It continues to take him in, and he continues to return to it for more.
sentences.zh: 它继续接纳他，而他也继续回到那里寻求更多。

sentences.en: In fact, there is reportedly only one person in the United States with more college degrees than Bulger, and the vast majority of those
sentences.zh: 事实上，据报道，美国只有一个人拥有的大学学位比博尔格多，而其中绝大多数

sentences.en: came from universities within the state of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 都来自密歇根州的大学。

sentences.en: No disrespect to the Broncos, Eagles, or Lakers.
sentences.zh: 并非对野马队、老鹰队或湖人队不敬。

sentences.en: Because Bulger is just 48, and Michael Nicholson of Kalamazoo is 83,
sentences.zh: 因为博尔格才48岁，而卡拉马祖的迈克尔·尼科尔森已经83岁了，

sentences.en: Bulger could surpass him, according to back-of-envelope math, as soon as 2054.
sentences.zh: 根据粗略计算，博尔格最早可能在2054年超过他。

sentences.en: In other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，

sentences.en: Bulger is on a plausible track to becoming the country's single-most-credentialed individual, at which point, perhaps, he could reSt.
sentences.zh: 博尔格有望成为全国拥有学位最多的人，到那时，也许他就能休息了。

sentences.en: A proposition.
sentences.zh: 一个命题。

sentences.en: No one more fully embodies the nature of elite American higher education today in all its contradictions than a man who has spent so much time being molded by it,
sentences.zh: 没有人比一个花了大把时间被其塑造、遵循其激励机制并内化其价值观的人，更能体现当今美国精英高等教育的本质及其所有矛盾了。

sentences.en: following its incentives and internalizing its values.
sentences.zh: 但这些价值观到底是什么？

sentences.en: But what are those values exactly?
sentences.zh: 当然，人们经常提到传统的优点，即花几年时间远离世界，阅读和思考。

sentences.en: Of course, there are the oft-cited traditional virtues of spending several years set apart from the rest of the world reading and thinking.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是拓展思维、挑战先入之见并培养学习热情的机会。

sentences.en: You know, the chance to expand your mind, challenge your preconceptions, and cultivate a passion for learning.
sentences.zh: 在这种愿景中，渴望知识的头脑被召唤到伟大的机构中以发挥其智力潜能，我们知道这些机构能够发挥这种功能，

sentences.en: In this vision, eager minds are called to great institutions to reach their intellectual potential, and we know these institutions can perform this function
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为它们被称为

sentences.en: Harvard and Yale.
sentences.zh: 对于某些人来说，精英教育可能就是这样运作的，但对大多数人来说可能并非如此。

sentences.en: That may be the way a prestigious education works for some, but probably not moSt.

sentences.zh: 41%的人正在进入咨询或金融行业。

sentences.en: 41% were entering careers in consulting or finance.
sentences.zh: 同样比例的人毕业时的起薪至少为11万美元，是全国中位数的两倍多。

sentences.en: The same percentage were graduating to a starting salary of at least $110,000, more than double the national median.
sentences.zh: 去年，斯坦福大学最受欢迎的专业是经济学和计算机科学。

sentences.en: Last year, the most popular majors at Stanford were economics and computer science.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，大学的终极价值在于证书，它保证了你在世俗成功阶梯上能向上攀升好几级。

sentences.en: The ultimate value of college for many is the credential, guaranteeing a starting spot many rungs up the ladder of worldly success.
sentences.zh: 你在精英大学学到的任何东西，都不如你花了几十万美元才写在简历上的那一行字重要。

sentences.en: Nothing you learn at an elite university is as important as the line on your CV that you've paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to type.
sentences.zh: 如果你持怀疑态度，你可能会争辩说，你申请大学所花费的时间，对你余生的影响比你在那里发生的任何具体事情都要大。

sentences.en: And if you were feeling cynical, you could argue that the time you spend applying to college will affect the rest of your life more than anything in particular
sentences.zh: “只有当我们忘记了所学，我们才开始真正了解，”

sentences.en: that happens while you're there.
sentences.zh: 梭罗在他进行简单生活实验后曾有名言。

sentences.en: It is only when we forget our learning that we begin to know,
sentences.zh: 尽管梭罗很富有，但他还是去了哈佛。

sentences.en: Thoreau observed famously after his experiment in simple living.
sentences.zh: 以一种截然不同、完全相反的方式，一种涉及中央供暖的方式，

sentences.en: Though rich of Thoreau, he went to Harvard.
sentences.zh: 博尔格在过去三十年里一直在进行他自己那半疯狂的美国教育实验。

sentences.en: In a much different, much opposed way, one involving central heat,
sentences.zh: 他比几乎任何人都更深地汲取了大学的精髓。

sentences.zh: 他知道些什么？

sentences.en: He was basically fine, but his parents were seriously injured, and his mother, Loretta, spent months in the hospital, ending up with a metal plate in one of her legs.
sentences.zh: 博尔格父母的婚姻破裂了。

sentences.en: She had to leave her job as a school teacher.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲有时很难相处，而他的父亲，一位在糟糕的离婚诉讼中为自己辩护的工程师兼专利律师，则对他进行情感虐待。

sentences.en: Bulger's parents' marriage disintegrated.
sentences.zh: 博尔格和母亲开始在弗林特附近的舒适住所和祖父在格兰德黑文的破旧农场之间轮流居住，那里四处漏风，

sentences.en: His mother could be difficult, and his father, an engineer and patent lawyer who represented himself during the nasty divorce, was emotionally abusive.
sentences.zh: 他们有时蜷缩在烧木头的炉子旁取暖。

sentences.en: Bulger and his mother began splitting time between their comfortable home near Flint and his grandfather's ramshackle farm in Grand Haven, which was so drafty
sentences.zh: 博尔格的母亲在随后的监护权争夺战中花光了大部分积蓄，而她儿子的严重阅读障碍使她的压力雪上加霜。

sentences.en: they sometimes curled up by the wood-burning furnace.
sentences.zh: 在三年级时，当博尔格还不会阅读时，他的老师说他高中都毕不了业。

sentences.en: Bulger's mother spent much of her money in the ensuing custody battle, and her stress was worsened by her son's severe dyslexia.
sentences.zh: 母亲意识到她的孩子很聪明，只是与众不同，于是决定在家教育他，尽管“家”这个词可能并不准确。

sentences.en: In third grade, when Bulger still couldn't read, his teachers said he wouldn't graduate from high school.
